newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks surge in buoyant trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks surge in buoyant trade.

text.p: Croatian shares, led by blue chips, surged ahead in upbeat trade on Wednesday, and traders said strong demand would keep prices high.
Leading Croatian drug firm Pliva gained 15 kuna to close at 490 on the day's record volume of 8,788 shares.
"It is a significant rise on such a high volume. The demand for the stock is still high, which is likely to keep the price up," Josko Milisa of I.C.F. borkerage said.
Pliva also rose in London, where its GDRs, issued five for each share, traded over $16 on Wednesday.

But traders saw the main reason for Pliva's and Zagrebacka Banka's strength in the investor interest in collecting the dividend, which both companies are due to pay out in June after shareholders' meetings.
Zagrebacka gained 22.5 kuna to close at 2,183, on the second-biggest volume of 4,762 shares.
Well-informed sources said on Tuesday that Zagrebacka may shelve plans to issue Eurobonds this spring because of a good chance to tap the syndicated loan at better terms.

"This means that they will get even cheaper money and further strengthen their position on the domestic market," Milisa said. The bank said on Monday it would lower its lending rates to prime borrowers for two percentage points.

Its preferred E-series issue, which carries a guaranteed 7-percent dividend but is traded in the semi-regulated segment of the Zagreb bourse, gained 20 kuna to 1,080 on relatively high volume of 775 shares.
"I expect the E-series stocks to close the gap somewhat on the ordinary share," Milisa said.
The bank's bearer stock was the biggest decliner, losing 20 kuna to 830 with only six shares sold.
Of other heavily traded stocks, food concern Podravka gained one kuna to 305 on the volume of 2,364 shares.
Biggest gainer textile firm Varteks added five kuna or 6.3 percent to 85, on volume of 500 units.
Traders said it was due to the company's announcement, made Tuesday, that the U.S. giant Levi Strauss & Co. would extend its licence for producing jeans for another five years.
Fifteen of 18 active issues rose, two fell and one was flat. Volume rose to 18,848 units, turnover to 16.5 million kuna from 14.2 on Tuesday.
"May could be an interesting month," another trader said.
